Week-by-week (12 weeks): Weeks 1–2 — finalize IRB‑approved materials, train coordinators/outreach nurse on standardized consent and teach‑back, confirm daily huddle times and webinar logistics, print multilingual flyers; Weeks 3–6 — begin active clinic screening blocks, one weekly clinic education session, host co‑hosted webinar in week 4, track screens/approaches/consents weekly; Weeks 7–9 — analyze two‑week yields, reallocate staff toward higher‑yield clinics, run targeted community outreach events and a second webinar if needed; Weeks 10–12 — prioritize follow‑up of screened patients, offer extended 30‑minute consent appointments, complete final outreach push, compile closeout metrics and escalate remaining barriers to the PI/sponsor.  
Concise teach‑back consent script (use aloud and record checklist items): “Thank you for your interest — this study [brief purpose sentence]. If you join, here’s what will happen (procedures, time commitment), the possible benefits and the known risks, alternatives including getting standard care without the study, how your data will be kept private, and that participation is completely voluntary and you may stop at any time; would you like time to think or to talk with a family member or your clinician?”  
Three teach‑back prompts to use immediately after explanation: “In your own words, what will you be asked to do if you join?”; “Can you tell me the main risks or side effects and any possible benefits?”; “If you wanted to stop, what would you do and who would you call?” (If responses are incomplete, re‑explain and reassess.)  
One‑page flyer text (IRB‑ready draft — adjust logos/contact info): Title: “[Study Name]: Volunteer Opportunity at [Hospital Name]”; Body bullets: “Who: adults/patients who [key eligibility in plain language]; Purpose: to study [brief neutral purpose]; What participation involves: [procedures], total time [X] visits/approx. time; Risks/benefits: there may be risks (list common, short) and possible benefits (may or may not directly benefit you); Alternatives: you may receive standard care instead; Compensation: as described in the consent (IRB‑approved); To learn more: attend our webinar on [date/time] or call [Site Research Line] or scan QR to register; Materials available in [languages]; Participation is voluntary and IRB‑approved.”
